key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can uniquely fingerprint and quantify grain-boundary defect species in organic halide perovskites, turning a traditionally qualitative probe into a direct defect meter.
engineering_relevance: This enables non-contact, room-temperature, closed-loop defect control for perovskite solar-cell processing and passivation, with the goal of improving stability and efficiency.
method: Measured THz-TDS spectra (0.3–3.0 THz) of SVE-fabricated MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3 thin films.
Matched intrinsic phonon modes and grain-boundary-localized molecular defect vibrations to build species-specific THz fingerprints.
Used oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and guide defect elimination strategies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting quantitative defect sensing.
watch_item: The approach depends on a robust THz fingerprint library and careful separation of defect signals from intrinsic phonon features, which may be material- and fabrication-dependent.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
